classification.difficultyReason: Use the supplied row and column headings and example cells to record ordered colour pairs, retaining repeated headings for distinct counters.

inlines.text: One bag contains 1 red counter, 2 yellow counters and 1 blue counter. Another bag contains 1 yellow counter, 2 red counters and 1 blue counter. One counter is taken at random from each bag. Copy and complete the following array to show all the possible outcomes for this experiment.

answer.worked:
Write the first-bag colour first and the second-bag colour second. Retain both R columns and both Y rows because they represent distinct counters.

R row: $(\mathrm{R},\mathrm{R}), (\mathrm{R},\mathrm{R}), (\mathrm{R},\mathrm{Y}), (\mathrm{R},\mathrm{B})$.

First Y row: $(\mathrm{Y},\mathrm{R}), (\mathrm{Y},\mathrm{R}), (\mathrm{Y},\mathrm{Y}), (\mathrm{Y},\mathrm{B})$.

Second Y row: $(\mathrm{Y},\mathrm{R}), (\mathrm{Y},\mathrm{R}), (\mathrm{Y},\mathrm{Y}), (\mathrm{Y},\mathrm{B})$.

B row: $(\mathrm{B},\mathrm{R}), (\mathrm{B},\mathrm{R}), (\mathrm{B},\mathrm{Y}), (\mathrm{B},\mathrm{B})$.

There are $4\times4=16$ counter-pair outcomes.
